title: How will Manchester Pride be different this year?

evidence_packet.title: How will Manchester Pride be different this year?
evidence_packet.lead: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
evidence_packet.summary: A new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC) has taken over running of the four-day event
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The August bank holiday weekend has been home to Manchester Pride for more than 40 years From its humble beginnings in 1985 as a fundraiser for Monsall Hospital's HIV and Aids ward, Manchester Pride grew into one of the country's biggest LGBTQ+ events When the company behind it went into voluntary liquidation last year, many were worried there would be no Pride in 2026 But Manchester City Council tried to allay fears when, in January, it announced that a new not-for-profit community interest company (CIC), Manchester Village Pride, would take over the running of the four-day event Manchester Village Pride is run by volunteer directors and is mainly made up of businesses from Manchester's Gay Village Venues in the area have loaned the new organisation £120,000 to support the planning and delivery of the event

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport is expecting around half a million passengers this bank holiday
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Passengers travelling through Manchester Airport over the August bank holiday weekend have been warned to check how they pack to help reduce delays during one of the busiest weekends in the airport's history The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) has urged travellers to avoid packing battery-powered devices in hold luggage as they pose a fire risk It said bags may have to be offloaded if items such as vapes and power banks are found in them About two million passengers are expected to depart from airports across Great Britain during the weekend, according to the regulator Anthony Shaw, a security team leader in the airport's hold baggage screening team, said staff often find devices including vapes, power banks and tablets in checked luggage "If the battery gets too hot, or is faulty, it can catch fire without warning," he said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford to extend long-term home-building plans - BBC News Image caption, Mike McCusker is the council's lead member for planning By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago Members of the public are being invited to have their say about plans to build nearly 35,000 new homes in Salford over the next 17 years - while also protecting the city's greenery. Extending the council's home-building plans by four years, a new document has sets out where new homes, jobs and infrastructure could be built until 2043. Deputy mayor and planning boss Mike McCusker said: "We will have a brand new development plan, which will give us a good pipeline of new homes as well as protection from developers, who could successfully appeal against planning applications which the council has rejected. "At the same time its important to protect our valuable green spaces for local people." Salford Council's existing local plan, which is part of the Greater Manchester-wide Places For Everyone strategy, outlines sites to be developed until 2039. Image caption, The draft local plan outlines the ambition to build warehouses on empty land next to the Salford Community Stadium The city has been one of the fastest growing in the UK over recent years, with its population rising to 294,000 in 2024 - an increase of 34% since 2001. Most of that growth has been in the city centre - and at Salford Quays - but there have also been new homes built on former green belt land in areas like Boothstown. Councillors will vote on the draft local plan before the end of this year and it will then be submitted to the government for final approval. Manchester Airports Group (MAG), which owns Manchester, East Midlands and London Stansted airports, said customers' contact details, vehicle registrations and postcodes were obtained by hackers at the weekend. MAG told the BBC the hackers demanded a ransom fee for the return of the data, which the group said it refused to pay. The sum of the ransom fee was not disclosed. The firm said "at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised" and the system hacked did not hold customers' bank or payment details. The data of about 8.7 million customers was accessed. The majority of the data accessed was restricted to customer email addresses and related to WiFi sign-ups within the airports' terminals, MAG said. MAG said in a statement: "We would like to reassure customers that Manchester Airport Group takes the security of customer information extremely seriously and we apologise for any inconvenience or concern caused." title: Speed limits and lane closures for M6 viaduct upgrade works

evidence_packet.title: Speed limits and lane closures for M6 viaduct upgrade works
evidence_packet.lead: Work will begin on replacing the M6 Thelwall Viaduct's joints on 1 September
evidence_packet.summary: Work will begin on replacing the M6 Thelwall Viaduct's joints on 1 September
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Speed limits and lane closures for M6 viaduct upgrade works - BBC News Image source, Anthony O'Neill/Geograph Image caption, The viaduct's joints have "reached the end of their operational lifespan", National Highways says By Georgie Docker North West Published 27 August 2026 Speed limits and lane closures are being imposed on a motorway viaduct as work is carried out to replace its bridge joints. The £27m "essential" upgrade will begin on the Thelwall Viaduct on the M6 in Lymm, Warrington, on 1 September. A full time contraflow system will be introduced from 12 October, as well as a temporary 40 mph (64 kmh) speed limit and narrow lanes. National Highways said the viaduct, which crosses the Manchester Ship Canal and the River Mersey, was "built several decades ago" and the work was needed for safety reasons. Work will be done on one carriage way at a time. Image source, Peter McDermott/Geograph Image caption, Work will be carried out overnight All lanes - northbound and southbound - will stay open during the day, with one lane open overnight on the carriageway being worked on. "Our road network is ageing, and many key structures, including Thelwall Viaduct, were built several decades ago," Chris Court from National Highways said. "The viaduct's joints have now reached the end of their operational lifespan, making replacement essential to maintain safety and reliability for road users." The project is due to be completed by the beginning of 2028. title: Swinton Park Golf Club: 700 homes proposed for former course

evidence_packet.title: Swinton Park Golf Club: 700 homes proposed for former course
evidence_packet.lead: Residents are being asked for views on a scheme including public open space and sports facilities
evidence_packet.summary: Residents are being asked for views on a scheme including public open space and sports facilities
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Swinton Park Golf Club: 700 homes proposed for former course - BBC News Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, The former Swinton Park Golf Club site has been closed since September 2020 By Charlotte Hall , Local Democracy Reporting Service and Haider Saleem , Reporting from North West Published 27 August 2026 Proposals for about 700 homes on a former golf course have raised residents‘ concerns about traffic and pressure on local services. Wain Estates is consulting on the future of the 100-acre former Swinton Park Golf Club site in Swinton, Greater Manchester, which closed in September 2020. The developer said more than half the site could become public open space, with affordable homes, sports facilities and housing for older people also proposed. But Mike Hartney, 65, who has lived in the area for 34 years, said traffic was already "awful" and local services were oversubscribed. "Everywhere is oversubscribed already," he said. "It'll only get worse." Wain Estates said it intended to seek outline planning permission later in 2026 and the number of homes could change following technical work, public feedback and discussions with council planners. Image source, Local Democracy Reporting Service Image caption, Mike Hartney said traffic and local services were already under pressure Dave Marsh, who was a member of the golf club for more than 30 years, said the course should be restored. Mr Marsh, who campaigns with Save Swinton Park Golf Club, said the grounds had remained closed throughout the coronavirus pandemic, despite appeals from the community. "It never should have closed as a golf club," he said. "We will fight it until our last breath to stop them." However, not all residents opposed developing the land. Image source, Local Democracy Repo

title: Burst pipe floods Scarisbrick restaurant for second time in three years

evidence_packet.title: Burst pipe floods Scarisbrick restaurant for second time in three years
evidence_packet.lead: United Utilities apologises after a Scarisbrick restaurant, which was flooded in 2023, is deluged again
evidence_packet.summary: United Utilities apologises after a Scarisbrick restaurant, which was flooded in 2023, is deluged again
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A restaurant owner has said he got "deja vu" when he was told one of his venues had been flooded after a water pipe burst for the second time in three years Salique Meah, 38, was alerted by one of his employees at Nellie Restaurant and Bar in Scarisbrick, Lancashire, at about 03:00 BST on Tuesday He said the venue was previously flooded on 26 June 2023 but this time the damage was worse, with the water up to 3ft (0.9m) in places, and there was not a single thing that he could salvage Water firm United Utilities apologised to the owners of three properties who had been affected by the flooding - which was caused by a burst water main- and said it was supporting them Meah, from Oldham, said there was "lots of water everywhere in the building" and it would cost "a lot" in terms of lost business He said he had to close the restaurant for 10 months last time this happened

title: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston

evidence_packet.title: Fans share memories of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston
evidence_packet.lead: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
evidence_packet.summary: Hundreds of fans went to Robin Park Arena to sign a book of condolence for the Wigan Warriors star
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fans have shared memories of the much-loved rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston and signed a book of condolence at his former club Wigan Warriors Rugby league's first knight died earlier this week aged 92 surrounded by his closest family, the club said As well as his achievements on the pitch - including scoring 571 tries in his career - a total surpassed only by Australian legend Brian Bevan in top-class rugby league - Boston has a legion of fans heartbroken at the legend's death The club's kitman, and a lifelong fan who first saw him as a child, and decades later worked for him in his pub when he retired, were among hundreds who went to Robin Park Arena to pay tribute to the star Josie Andrews held back the tears as she told BBC North West Tonight : "I fell in love with Billy Boston when I was eight "My dad took me to watch him and that is when I fell in love with Wigan rugby."

Hackers accessed data relating to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI s The data included people's email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes. The group said 'at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised' during the incident and neither MAG nor the system hacked held customers’ bank or payment detail Today people affected are receiving emails about the hack. The email says: "We're contacting you about a recent cyber security incident involving customer data "Our investigation has identified that some of your personal information relating to airport car parking, lounge, Fast Track bookings and on-airport WIFI sign-ups has been accessed by an unauthorised third party."

evidence_packet.title: Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extens
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extens
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extension built without planning permission at a former bank have been ordered to be ripped down In the past few months three metal lean-to shutters have been installed along the side of the former NatWest building on the corner of Church Street, Farnworth, along with an extension. Bolton council has said no planning permission was previously applied for or approved for the The enforcement notice, published by the council, states that subject to any appeal being lodged, the unauthorised extension must be demolished and the roller shutter doors must be removed within two months of notice taking effect on September 30 A third condition of the enforcement notice states: “Restore the south principal elevation of the building to its condition immediately before the unauthorised development took place “This includes but is not limited to, the repair of the original elevation removed or damaged during the construction works using materials to match the original building in appearance, colour, texture and finish.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Solar Eclipse Will you have clear skies for the lunar eclipse? Check your postcode Stargazers across the country could catch a glimpse of the celestial event as the Sun, Earth and Moon align, causing the Earth to cast its shadow across the lunar surfa People in Manchester will have the chance to see the Moon turn an eerie shade of red in the early hours of Friday as a spectacular lunar eclipse takes place over the UK Stargazers across the country could catch a glimpse of the celestial event as the Sun, Earth and Moon align, causing the Earth to cast its shadow across the lunar surface The deep partial lunar eclipse will take place in the early hours of August 28, when around 93% of the Moon is expected to be covered by the darkest part of Earth's shadow at the peak of the event But whether people will actually be able to see the eclipse will depend heavily on the weather , with cloud cover expected to threaten views in several parts of the UK The Met Office has warned that "conditions are expected to be challenging for many hoping to see the eclipse", although southern and eastern England are expected to have the best chance of catching at least part of the spectacle

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Trafford council could lose control of children's services after seven years of 'failure' 'They do not get their childhood back while we improve the process' Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:14, 27 Aug 2026 View 3 Images An emergency counci Trafford council could lose control of children’s services as the government steps in to deal with the crisis-hit department A recent Ofsted inspection saw the service rated ‘inadequate’ by the education watchdog , the lowest possible rating. Inspectors found children were being left in ‘potentially unsafe situations for too long’ because of delays in initial responses Some of the problems identified by inspectors were branded ‘serious and significant’, and in some cases ‘unrealistic expectations’ were being placed on children ‘to keep themselves safe’. Town hall bosses did not ‘fully’ grasp the extent of the issues until they were pointed out Council leadership apologised for the failings found in the service, saying work to improve the services is under way and thanking staff for their professionalism and commitment Just a week later, the council received a second critical report, this time into its Adult Social Care department . Healthcare inspectors from the Care Quality Commission found long waits; low satisfaction; and ‘ineffective’ sharing of safeguarding lessons but noted improvements

title: Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission

evidence_packet.title: Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extens
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extens
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Changes to former Bolton NatWest bank ordered to be torn down after being built without permission Planning enforcement has been instigated at a former NatWest building which dates back to Victorian times Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy Metal shutters and an extension built without planning permission at a former bank have been ordered to be ripped down In the past few months three metal lean-to shutters have been installed along the side of the former NatWest building on the corner of Church Street, Farnworth, along with an extension. Bolton council has said no planning permission was previously applied for or approved for the The enforcement notice, published by the council, states that subject to any appeal being lodged, the unauthorised extension must be demolished and the roller shutter doors must be removed within two months of notice taking effect on September 30 A third condition of the enforcement notice states: “Restore the south principal elevation of the building to its condition immediately before the unauthorised development took place “This includes but is not limited to, the repair of the original elevation removed or damaged during the construction works using materials to match the original building in appearance, colour, texture and finish.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham Andy Burnham sparks political row as he says Irish unity poll ‘off the table’ The Prime Minister was making his first visit to Northern Ireland since taking office Comments News Jonathan McCambridge , Claudia Savage , Rebecca Black and Am Andy Burnham has sparked a political row during his first visit to Northern Ireland as Prime Minister after he stated that an Irish border poll is “off the table” Sinn Féin leader Mary Lou McDonald reacted strongly to the remarks, stating that no prime minister has the right to “high-handedly” remove the provision for a unity referendum from the Good Friday Agreement However, DUP leader Gavin Robinson welcomed the comments, stating the Prime Minister had “put to bed the nonsense” speculation over a unity poll, the Press Association reports During his visit to Belfast Mr Burnham said he is “here to listen” but added that the “rifts” arising from referendums “take a long time to heal”, referring to Brexit and the Scottish independence referendum Under the terms of the 1998 Belfast/Good Friday Agreement, the Secretary of State can decide to hold a border poll, and it also places a duty on the office holder to call one if it appears likely a majority would vote for Irish unification

Check your postcode Stargazers across the country could catch a glimpse of the celestial event as the Sun, Earth and Moon align, causing the Earth to cast its shadow across the lunar surfa People in Manchester will have the chance to see the Moon turn an eerie shade of red in the early hours of Friday as a spectacular lunar eclipse takes place over the UK Stargazers across the country could catch a glimpse of the celestial event as the Sun, Earth and Moon align, causing the Earth to cast its shadow across the lunar surface The deep partial lunar eclipse will take place in the early hours of August 28, when around 93% of the Moon is expected to be covered by the darkest part of Earth's shadow at the peak of the event But whether people will actually be able to see the eclipse will depend heavily on the weather , with cloud cover expected to threaten views in several parts of the UK The Met Office has warned that "conditions are expected to be challenging for many hoping to see the eclipse", although southern and eastern England are expected to have the best chance of catching at least part of the spectacle

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Why millions of people are getting emails from Manchester Airport today Around 8.7 million people's data has been accessed in a hack at the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter Millions of people have recei
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Why millions of people are getting emails from Manchester Airport today Around 8.7 million people's data has been accessed in a hack at the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter Millions of people have received emails from the Manchester Airports Group (MAG) following a major cyber hack The company, which operates Manchester Airport , London Stansted and East Midlands Airport, has sent emails to the 8.7 million customers affected by the data breach earlier this week. Hackers accessed data relating to car park, lounge and fast track bookings and in-airport WIFI s The data included people's email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registrations and postcodes. The group said 'at no point has passenger safety or aviation security been compromised' during the incident and neither MAG nor the system hacked held customers’ bank or payment detail Today people affected are receiving emails about the hack. The email says: "We're contacting you about a recent cyber security incident involving customer data "Our investigation has identified that some of your personal information relating to airport car parking, lounge, Fast Track bookings and on-airport WIFI sign-ups has been accessed by an unauthorised third party."

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Ross Mackenzie, who founded the Liars Club Group/ Crazy Pedro’s and built and sold the Black Dog Ballroom bars, has taken ownership of Nuthurst Day Care on Nuthurst Road. The nur
evidence_packet.evidence_text: One of Manchester’s best-known hospitality operators has taken on a children’s nursery in New Moston Ross Mackenzie, who founded the Liars Club Group/ Crazy Pedro’s and built and sold the Black Dog Ballroom bars, has taken ownership of Nuthurst Day Care on Nuthurst Road. The nursery opens in September for children aged six months to five years It is an unlikely move for a man who has spent three decades in licensed retail, and Mackenzie is the first to say so On this new move, he commented; “Hospitality and childcare have more in common than people assume. Both come down to people walking through your door and trusting you with a few hours of their day. The stakes are just very different, and I don’t take that lightly “I’ve spent thirty years building places people actually want to be in. I want Nuthurst to be that for the families of New Moston.” The nursery, at 204 Nuthurst Road, has been fully refurbished up over the summer ahead of the September opening. It has three rooms, named Hedgehogs, Squirrels and Owls, and a large garden overlooking Nuthurst Park

Within days she was placed in an induced coma and transferred to the specialist liver intensive care unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham, one of only a handful of c On 22 July a donor liver became available, but during the operation she suffered three cardiac arrests after a blood clot blocked the main artery to her lungs, leaving her starved of oxygen for a prolonged period. Surgeons told her husband Ollie more than once that she was unlike Against the odds she pulled through. Six weeks on she is conscious and recognises her family, but the lack of oxygen caused significant brain damage to both sides of her brain. She cannot move, remains on a ventilator and dialysis, and is still in critical care “She’s conscious. She is recognising who we are,” Ollie said. “She’s saying the odd word, albeit very, very weak. She can’t move or anything like that at the moment. They’re hopeful of a form of recovery, but whether she will walk again remains unknown.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: There’s a cruelty to Mike Rice, a wickedness. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Newcastle United have signed Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez for a fee which could rise to £52m The Spaniard has joined the club on a long-term contract after completing his medical on Tyneside "I'm really happy to be here at this amazing club," he said. evidence_packet.summary: Manchester United are set to lose a young star to Arsenal this summer on a free transfer, as he bids farewell to the Reds on social media
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United Transfer News Man Utd player bids emotional farewell with transfer confirmation set Manchester United are set to lose a young star to Arsenal this summer on a free transfer, as he bids farewell to the Reds on social media Comments Sport Scott Trot Habeeb Ogunneye looks set to complete a switch to Arsenal after bidding farewell to Manchester United . The defender has indicated it is time to move on after paying tribute to the Reds The 20-year-old spent five years progressing through the academy at Old Trafford but is poised to relocate to north London on a free transfer, with United reportedly securing a substantial sell-on clause in the arrangement. Reds team-mate James Scanlon is expected to make the ide Arsenal's new Under-21s head coach, David Horseman, knows both players well, having previously worked at United as an academy coach. Ogunneye, a right-back, was understood to have completed a medical before his transfer earlier this week Writing on Instagram, the youngster said: "Five years. What a journey. Forever grateful for the memories, the people and everything this club has given me. Time for the next chapter." FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! evidence_packet.evidence_text: Events EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters EU €3 Customs Duty Rule 2026: What This Means for UK Exporters Official Chamber Post FREE Online Thursday 10 Sep 10am - 11am Book Now About the event The way low-value goods enter the European Union is changing From 1 July 2026, the EU introduced a new €3 customs duty on low-value consignments valued up to €150 entering the EU from outside the bloc. The change removes the previous duty exemption and introduces new considerations for businesses exporting goods directly to EU customers The new duty applies based on product categories/tariff classifications rather than simply per parcel, meaning shipments containing different types of goods could face multiple charges. For example, a parcel containing products under different tariff headings may attract multiple While the change is aimed largely at addressing the growth of low-value e-commerce imports, it will also impact UK businesses selling products directly into EU markets, including online retailers, brands and SMEs What the new €3 EU customs duty means for UK businesses
